newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: AIRPORT LEASES SOLD FOR A$3.3 BILLION
The Federal Government has sold the leases for airports in Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth for around three point three billion dollars.
The highest amount was paid by the Brisbane Airport Corporation Ltd for the Brisbane airport ..at a price of nearly one point-four billion dollars.
Australian Pacific Airports Corporation paid one point three billion dollars for the Melbourne airport ..and Airspace Development Group paid nearly 650 million dollars for the Perth airport.
The Government says it's very pleased with the outcome ..and all three airports will be majority Australian owned.
LABOR FORMALLY MOVES FOR SENATE COMMITTEE ON COLSTON
Labor's Senate Leader, John Faulkner, says allegations that Senator Mal Colston misled the Upper House are among the most serious cases of Parliamentary abuse he's ever come across.
Senator Faulkner's claim came as the Opposition formally moved to have a Senate Committee investigate the allegations, surrounding the wrongful claiming of Senator Colston's travel expenses.
The ALP and the Greens have been pushing for the Privileges Committee to investigate the matter.
DODSON SAYS NATS TAKING WRONG APPROACH ON NATIVE TITLE
Aboriginal Social Justice Commissioner, Mick Dodson, says the National Party's taking the wrong approach in its rejection of the Federal Government's native title plan.
The National Party federal management committee has declared the ten-point plan unacceptable, because it doesn't extinguish native title on pastoral leases.
Mr Dodson says over the past 200 years Aboriginal people have lost enough of their property rights, and now the Nationals want to take what's left.
DEMOCRATS FORCE CHANGES TO SUPER SURCHARGE SCHEME
Democrats Senator, Lyn Allison, says the Federal Government's agreement to accept changes to superannuation surcharge proposals will protect the most vulnerable people.
Senator Allison says people who lose their jobs, and those on low incomes, could have been caught up in the scheme as it was proposed by the Government.
But she says this will be avoided when the Government agrees to a Democrat amendment which will ensure redundancy payments will not be counted as income in determining who has to pay the levy.
The 15 percent surcharge will apply to the super contributions of people earning more than 70-thousand dollars.
OPPOSITION CONDEMNS SMITH'S APPOINTMENT TO CASA
The Federal Opposition says the appointment of Dick Smith as Deputy Chairman of the Civil Aviation Safety Authority Board is a repayment for his political and financial support of the Coalition.
The aviator and businessman was appointed, along with aviation engineer, Laurence Foley, to new specially created Board positions.
Shadow Transport spokesman, Lindsay Tanner, says Mr Smith's appointment will lead to disruption and serious disputes within CASA.
Mr Tanner says he represents a particular set of sectional interests and hardline views which aren't shared by the bulk of the aviation industry.
Transport Minister, John Sharp, concedes that while Mr Smith has his detrators, he has extensive experience and the appropriate qualifications for the job.
NEW LEAGUE TO KEEP SWIMMERS IN TOP-FORM ALL YEAR ROUND
A new national swimming league has been set up to help keep Australian swimmers at the world forefront.
National Swimming Coach Don Talbot has devised the round-robin competition, to help meet a shortfall of competitive swimming events during winter.
Graham Sampson, of South Australian Swimming, says there'll be six teams, comprising young, rising star and top level swimmers.
Mr Sampson says it gives Australian swimmers an opportunity to be competitive all year, and to maintain international performances.
He says it's competition they would only get if they were entering into national level competition like the Australian opens or major event selection trials.
